note: A break keeps its rhythm in beat-led places (his words 10-30: 'There's always some notion of rhythm throughout. Not necessarily a full drum set, but we can't lose the rhythm'; on the sketches: 'ideally should follow beat style, if it's straight then hats, if it's broken half time'; on Vibe - Solar Wind: 'all three options are nice, could we make it up to the birds to control the approach'). Read off the plan, never a genre: how beat-led the theme is (`beatLed`, the tempo as played), whether its groove is straight (the kick on all four beats) or broken, and which of its own drums it has. Under `bands.lift` the break stays beatless, as today. From it, the beatless stretch of every breakdown run (from its first bar to the first kick, backbeat or build the break already plays) keeps one carrier made of the theme's own sounds: the `hats` line (the groove's hat, thinned and high-passed, building into the drop), the `half-time` ghost (its own backbeat once a bar on 3, kickless and filtered, its ghosts and quartered hats), or the gentle `pump` (the bed's held notes breathing on the beat, a few dB, never a gate or a chop). From `bands.drive` the carrier builds over the stretch into the drop: its last quarter denser and opening; between the two it stays at its lightest throughout. The beat's style picks the default (`own`); the birds lean the others in where they fit (`leans`, the one lean, centred on the house: Spark's straight or broken beat, Tide's close or wide room, Loom's short or long form, Root's body); the pump has no weight of its own and comes only where the birds lean to it, or where it is the only carrier the theme has (a groove of the kick alone). One draw per theme off its own stream, so every break of a theme keeps the same carrier. A drum carrier is lifted inside the break only, to stand `level.target` dB under the bed as the plan reads both (each hit and each note as played, by its measured loudness per unit: the hats by `hat-scene.json`'s `keys.hats`, the bed and the backbeat by its `keysBody.scene`), never past `level.most` up or `level.least` down. Every number is a starting point for listening.

leans.says: the one lean (src/lean.ts), centred on the middle of each bird's range, on the carriers the beat's style did not pick (its own keeps its weight as written): Spark (the beat straight or broken) between the hats and the half-time; Tide (a close, dry room or a wide one) toward the hats or the pump; Loom (short loops or a long form) toward the hats or the half-time ghost; Root (the body) toward the pump. The pump is drawn only where its lean is over one

hats.says: the groove's own hat, each hit a copy of one it plays (at its step where it plays there, else its nearest of the same kind), on `steps`: `light` through a lift's stretch; a drive's first half on `first`, the next quarter on `second`, the last quarter (two bars at least) on `second` with the groove's sixteenth part on every sixteenth it plays; through a high-pass at `hp` (the last quarter's falling from its first to its second over the bars), `db` over the lift

halfTime.says: the groove's own backbeat once a bar on `backbeat` (beat 3), kickless and high-passed; at a drive its ghost strokes as the groove plays them and its hat on `hatSteps`; the last quarter lifts by `db.last` and its hat goes to every eighth; at a lift the backbeat alone

pump.says: the bed's held notes (a beat long or more) breathing on every beat, the house duck's shape written on the notes: down to `depthDb` at `minimumBeats`, `back` of the way up by `backBeats`, whole by `wholeBeats`; `depthDb` by stage (a lift's throughout; a drive's, then its last quarter's). Never deeper than a few dB, never a gate, never eighths

level.says: the carrier's lift inside the break: its main line's hits (the hats, or the backbeat) per `window` seconds over the stretch, against the bed's mean in a `window` from each beat (what sounds there besides the drums and the noises: the pad, the keys, the bass), each as the program plays it (the room's lane, the keyed floor, the stage, gain and velocity, the spell's seasoning) and by its loudness per unit (`hits` by voice, `beds` by class: a layer and its voice, a pad by its timbre; `hit` and `bed` one the table does not hold), in dB; the lift brings the line to `target` LU under the bed, never past `most`, never under `least`, in half decibels. The units are fitted (tmp lab of round break-pulse-rule) over 78 rendered breaks, the eight featured tracks that move and the beat-led tiles' seeds 1-4, each carrier and each bed rendered alone through the real graph: the bed's median miss 0.5 dB (most 4.7), the line over the bed's 1.4 dB (a hat whose room voices it longer or shorter misses by up to 10, the lift's bounds holding it audible and under the bed). The target: the sketches he heard stood the line 10-17 LU under the bed (Vibe - Solar Wind 10, Drive - Static Charge 12, Vibe - Undertow 17)

hold.says: Round break-hats (his ear 11-03 on a Chillstep track: 'in this break end the hats got very loud, and then the drop starts and the sound is quieter because of all the other voices ... one fix, to balance it in the break, so it will likely feel uniform when switching to the drop'). The carrier's hats at the stretch's end, its last `bars` (the plan's read: every hat of the carrier as lifted over the bed, the units above), stand no louder against the bed than the groove they land on keeps its hats against its mix (its first `bars`, `top-lanes.json` `level.read`, the hat-ceiling's read; `offsetDb` the one step between the two reads, measured on renders), so the hats keep their place against everything else from the break into the drop. The whole stretch comes down by that one cut, so the build still grows into the drop and lands on the groove's place; never raised, never under `least` against the bed (3 dB under the quietest line he heard keep a break, Vibe - Undertow's sketch at 17 LU under its bed). MEASURED (tools/break-hats.ts, 16 carried breaks into a groove in the Chillstep place, the beat-led featured and his track, rendered with the hats alone and the rest alone, K-weighted): the end's read lands 2.1 dB rms from the render, the groove's read 5.8 dB under it (the median; 4.0-7.9, Drive - Static Charge 9.4 under its closed lid), the jump the two read 2.5 dB rms from the rendered one: the five jumps of 4.9 dB or more read 4.4-10.4 dB, one of 4.1 read as none.
hold.intoSays: Round hat-top (11-03): the sections a carried break may land on and be held against. A theme's last break hands to its outro's drums as an earlier one hands to the drop, and was left as it was: measured (K-weighted, the hats alone against the rest), his Chillstep track's second breakdown ended 6.2 dB over its groove's place, Vibe - Undertow's second 11.4, Drive - Cloudburst's second 3.1, the very jump round break-hats took out at the drop. Take `outro` out and only the drop's and the main's seams are held.
hold.endMostSays: Round hat-top: the end is read against the bed it plays over, so an end whose hats stand over that bed (the bed gone from the break's last bars, the hats alone) gives no place to hold to and is left as drawn: one such end over the Map's grid, Dub Techno's second seed, whose last 32-bar break ends on the hats 2.2 dB over a bed that has left, and whose whole stretch the one cut would have taken 17.9 dB down, under every other sound of the break. No break the rule held before reads over nought.
